title: AI Workflows for Private Equity Portfolio Teams, Built on Your Firm's Record
summary: A knowledge graph for private equity connects your firm's deals, decisions, and relationships into one structured foundation. Metal's Context Graph is built for private capital, so every new deal starts with everything your firm has already learned.
body_markdown:
Metal provides five out-of-the-box workflows that cover Private Equity portfolio teams' work from the quarterly review to the exit decision. Each run reads from the firm's[Context Graph](https://www.metal.ai/blog/understanding-knowledge-graph) and writes its reviewed result back, so the next board meeting starts from a fuller record.


### What Does a Context Layer Change for Private Equity Portfolio Teams?


The work still happens. What changes is what each board meeting and exit decision is read against.


Metal brings your firm's investment record and judgment into every step: **the original thesis and IC case, the value creation plan, every board deck and set of minutes, and what management committed to quarter by quarter.**

### What Out-of-the-Box Workflows Does Metal Offer Private Equity Portfolio Teams?


Metal ships five out-of-the-box workflows, each built around a question the portfolio team has to answer between close and exit. The workflows all read from and write back to the same[Context Graph](https://www.metal.ai/blog/understanding-knowledge-graph) . Each one is shaped to the firm: its KPI definitions, board templates, and review steps.


When a process is unique to the firm, your team build the workflow in Metal's ***Workflow Builder*** , working alongside Metal to take it into production. The workflow stays the firm's own. Your team edits the steps, decides who approves each run, and can restore any earlier version.

#### Portfolio Monitoring: Catch What the Headline Number Hides


Portfolio Monitoring reads every board deck and financial file for a selected portfolio company, extracts the financial metrics across formats, and standardizes the KPIs to the firm's definitions. Teams can customize the template by adding their own fund-specific KPIs, thesis checkpoints, and LP reporting requirements.


What you get:


-


Revenue, EBITDA, and margin trends, with variance against budget and forecast


-


Retention and customer metrics, including ARR growth, NRR, churn, and customer concentration


-


Operating metrics tracked against the value creation plan


-


Red flags and outliers across the portfolio, before they become crises


-


Every flag traced to the board slide or financial statement behind it


A company growing revenue can still be losing its best customers. The review starts from the number that explains the headline, with the source attached.


#### Competitor Positioning Analysis: See Where the Company Stands Against Its Market


Competitor Positioning Analysis analyzes a portfolio company against its key competitors using recent news, M&A activity, and market signals to assess competitive positioning and momentum.


What you get:


-


A competitive momentum scorecard of the company and its top competitors


-


Scores on market share momentum, M&A execution, leadership stability, innovation and service expansion, and regulatory and compliance posture


-


Takeaways on where the company is strongest relative to its peers


-


A numbered citation on every finding, back to its source


The board reads the company's momentum against its market, not only against its own plan.


#### Board Meeting Prep: Walk In With the Questions That Matter


Board Meeting Prep prepares a strategic board meeting brief for a portfolio company by synthesizing quarterly board materials, value creation plans, and meeting minutes into a chairman-level discussion guide.


What you get:


-


An executive summary: key metrics against budget, what the board needs to focus on, and a headline recommendation


-


The quarterly trajectory, with management's commitments tracked against what was delivered and discrepancies across source documents flagged


-


The value creation plan assessed lever by lever, with the biggest win and the biggest gap


-


Strategic issues and risk flags, each with why it matters, what the data shows, and what to watch for


-


A discussion guide with time allocated per topic, questions for management, what a good answer looks like, and the red flag to listen for


The board meeting starts from what management said last quarter, what the numbers show this quarter, and where the two diverge.


#### Exit Readiness Assessment: Know Whether to Sell Now or Hold


Exit Readiness Assessment is a comprehensive exit readiness evaluation for a portfolio company, covering financial positioning, market timing, buyer universe, and remaining value creation runway.


What you get:


-


A readiness verdict and a recommended action, with a target exit timeline and route


-


The biggest factor supporting an exit now, and the biggest factor against it


-


Each dimension scored, from earnings quality and margin profile to revenue concentration and leverage


-


Performance read against the original IC case


-


A numbered citation on every finding, back to its source


The hold-or-sell conversation starts from what the firm underwrote and what the company has delivered since.


### How Accurately Does Metal Read Deal Documents?


In Metal's September 2026 evaluation, the same model and agent answered 51 questions over a real private equity dataset twice: once reading through Metal's context layer, once through a leading enterprise file platform, each via MCP.


-


Metal scored 95.1 out of 100 on quality versus 86.6.


-


On the 17 hardest questions, including EBITDA bridges and conflicting document versions, Metal scored 96.1 versus 83.1.


-


On the structured workflow questions, runs through Metal had 93% fewer tool errors: 1.4 failed tool calls per answer against 18.9.


-


Across all questions, Metal used 41% fewer tokens per answer.
